text:
Maria G.: heads up — planning a new default for model-version upgrades. want feedback on a staged traffic controller policy that is percent-step + dwell-time + telemetry guards. thinking defaults for percent steps and guard thresholds so teams don’t shoot themselves in the foot.

Sam K.: love it. can you sketch the defaults you have in mind?

Maria G.: initial thought: 0->1% (5m), 1->5% (15m), 5->20% (30m), 20->50% (1h), 50->100% (2h). guards: error-rate delta > 0.5pp OR p99 latency increase > 50ms triggers automatic pause + notify. rollback threshold if error-rate delta > 1.5pp within a step.

Devon: those numbers seem reasonable for high-traffic services. question: how do we handle low-traffic customers where 1% is < 100 requests? stepping by percent will be noisy.

Laura: for small traffic, we should support absolute-sample overrides (e.g., min-requests-per-step: 200) or a "log ramp" mode that increases by absolute counts rather than percent.

Sam K.: agreed. we should also surface estimated sample counts per step in the console before applying so the user knows the expected numbers.

Maria G.: good point. UI suggestion: when configuring rollout, show two modes: "percent" (default) and "sample-based". if percent mode and sample < min_samples, warn and suggest sample mode.

Devon: practicality: routing consistency for multi-turn sessions. need sticky assignment keyed by session_id/user_id so a user stays on the chosen model for duration of session. otherwise conversations flip between versions.

Laura: +1. also need to account for inference cache warming: new model might have colder KV cache causing latency blips at early steps. telemetry guard should use rolling median and exclude first N requests per model instance to avoid false positives.

Sam K.: ops question: what signals do we ingest for guards? error-rate, p50/p95/p99, token-consumption, inference-failure-types, model-assertions (e.g., decode-fail). also want a quality signal: eval-keyed prompts -> correctness/regression score.

Maria G.: plan: guards listen to: 1) request_error_rate, 2) p99_latency, 3) top-level quality_regression_score (from canary eval set), 4) business_telemetry (e.g., conversion-rate delta if available). each guard has threshold and severity (pause vs rollback).

Devon: Implementation note: telemetry lag — eval-based quality signal can be delayed. we should allow separate severity windows: immediate safety guards (errors/latency) and delayed quality guards (24h window) that can trigger rollback but not immediate pause.

Laura: UX: allow checkbox for "auto rollback on quality regression" and a separate slider for "rollback sensitivity" to avoid too many false positives.

Sam K.: edge case: split rounding. when traffic is tiny, percent allocation is effectively 0. ensure we implement floor allocation: each step must route at least 1 request per N users to guarantee visibility.

Maria G.: also thinking API shape for rollout config. example:

```json
{
  "strategy": "staged-percent",
  "steps": [
    {"percent": 1, "dwell": "5m"},
    {"percent": 5, "dwell": "15m"},
    {"percent": 20, "dwell": "30m"},
    {"percent": 50, "dwell": "1h"},
    {"percent": 100, "dwell": "2h"}
  ],
  "min_samples_per_step": 200,
  "guards": {
    "immediate": {"error_rate_delta_pp": 0.5, "p99_latency_ms": 50},
    "escalation": {"error_rate_delta_pp": 1.5}
  },
  "sticky_key": "session_id",
  "auto_rollback_on_quality": false
}
```

Devon: that looks good. small nit: use snake_case vs camelCase consistently across API. pick one. also include an explicit "dry_run" flag and a rollout_id so we can correlate telemetry.

Sam K.: and include an optional "preheat" boolean that tells routing to warm a small fleet of instances (e.g., 5%) to reduce cache-warmup artifacts.

Maria G.: +preheat option is smart. will add. we should also add a human-in-the-loop step: allow the console to pause at any step and require manual continue. default = auto-continue but orgs can choose manual.

ops-bot: deploy-bot started canary rollout 1769876543-rc2 -> will monitor metrics. (reacted with :eyes:)

Laura: monitoring/alerts: create standard dashboards per rollout that show step timeline, signal deltas, sample counts, and a small list of impacted API keys (so support can reach out).

Devon: and bake in an audit trail: each step transition records who/what triggered it, telemetry snapshot, and a link to the trace samples for quick debugging.

Sam K.: open question: do we want to allow multi-variant A/B as part of the same rollout? e.g., split 10% to v2a, 10% to v2b, rest v1. complexity goes up but it's useful for head-to-heads.

Maria G.: let's support it but behind an "advanced" toggle. default single-target rollout covers most use cases. multi-variant needs more sophisticated analytics.

Laura: ok — next steps: Maria will draft a concise RFC for defaults + API + console mockups. Sam/Devon will list telemetry events and min sample heuristics. I can mock dashboards.

Maria G.: thanks team. I’ll post the RFC in #eng-platform once ready. @Sam K. @Devon please add any missing gotchas here.

Sam K.: one more gotcha — billing/quotas: we must show estimated cost delta during rollout preview because running two models briefly inflates cost.

Devon: +1. include token-rate estimate and GPU-hour impact in preview.

Maria G.: noted. thanks! :thumbsup:
